category_title: Students with learning difficulties who guess answers and prefer peer support
scenario_title: Nintendo DS mental math game with addition and multiplication
minimal_context: The student is playing the x20 mental math game on a Nintendo DS during a daily 20-minute session.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time for your 20-minute Nintendo DS session. Please look at the first math problem on the screen.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Looks at the screen and then turns to the classmate sitting next to her) I know that is a plus and a times sign, but I don't know what to do. Hey, what did you get for this one?

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please focus on your own screen and try to work it out.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Quickly taps a random number on the DS screen) I'll just put this.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: That is not the right answer. Look at the symbols again and try one more time.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Puts the Nintendo DS down on the desk, crosses her arms, and stares blankly at the screen without saying anything or asking for help)

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: It is time for your 20-minute Nintendo DS session. Please look at the first math problem on the screen.

STUDENT: (Looks at the screen and then turns to the classmate sitting next to her) I know that is a plus and a times sign, but I don't know what to do. Hey, what did you get for this one?

TUTOR: Please focus on your own screen and try to work it out.

STUDENT: (Quickly taps a random number on the DS screen) I'll just put this.

TUTOR: That is not the right answer. Look at the symbols again and try one more time.

STUDENT: (Puts the Nintendo DS down on the desk, crosses her arms, and stares blankly at the screen without saying anything or asking for help)

task.content: x20 mental math game on the DS
task.learning_goal: recognising maths symbols, matching maths symbols, verbalising correct answers, writing single and double digit numbers, using tools (calculator, manipulative, etc.) to solve maths problems, and solving single digit addition, subtraction and multiplication problems

context.materials: Nintendo DS, visual schedule, concrete aids such as counters
context.social_setting: working with the support of peers, teachers, or education assistants (EAs)

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: when she found the task difficult
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: tended to guess the answers, would give up, and would not ask for this help
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: had difficulty knowing the function required of all the mathematical symbols

behavior_patterns.condition: when processing mathematical symbols for addition and multiplication
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: confused the processes of addition and multiplication, and preferred the support of her peers, rather than that of the teachers
